items.text: Patterns can change With the A | B swing: each time the crossfader swings over to the other side, the next pattern comes (Field pane, Patterns, Change).
Patterns can change With the dice: each roll of the dice brings the next pattern. By hand still works with the Next pattern button.
Better: Load G-code files and Paste G-code carry the G-code page icon from Current, the sister tool.
Patterns can change With the Form: each new movement of the performance brings the next pattern (Field pane, Patterns, Change).

Your own G-code as patterns: Load G-code files (plotter, laser or CNC files) or Paste G-code, and they go into a set called Mine, kept on this device. Anything with pen-down moves works; "Remove unticked" clears the ones you don't want.
Current's patterns as a set: Woven Diamond, Spiral Arc, Raster, Hatch and Rose.
Better: a pattern at rest is drawn at full detail, however many strokes it has; its points for the sounds and the changes are spread evenly along the whole drawing.

Patterns in the field. A pattern set comes in the way a sound set does: the first is Astrology, in two groups, Signs (the twelve glyphs, drawn as clean geometric lines) and Constellations (the twelve star figures). Tick one, some or all; Bag random plays each ticked pattern once in a shuffled order, or choose In order, or Stay on one. Change by hand (Next pattern, or hold a pattern to play it now) or every 20, 45 or 90 seconds. Field pane, Patterns.
The pattern moves on its own, apart from the sounds: Still, Turn, Drift, Breathe or Wander, at the size you set.

A change of pattern is a sonic moment: every vertex flattens onto one line through the middle (across, up and down, or taking turns), holds while the line keeps turning, then opens into the next pattern. Sounds held on the pattern line up along it and sweep round with it.

Each sound has its own way of going with the pattern: Free (as before), Still (held at its vertex, so it moves when the pattern moves), Wander (drifts around its vertex) or Follow (travels along the lines). New sounds take the choice in the pane; hold a sound for its own.
The field's drifting marks follow the pattern's lines, gently or strongly.

Speakers: 2, 4, 8 or headphones, with you in the middle of the floor, so a piece can be made for four or eight speakers. On a device with fewer outputs the pane says what is really heard. Two speakers keep the field exactly as before.

Fixed: the Scatter line-up had no icon at all in the line-up list, and Orbit showed as a bare circle. Their dots were drawn as zero-length lines, which some screens do not paint. They are real dots now.

Fixed: the A | B line's motion did not move when the robot was off, because its beats and bars only counted while the robot played. They now run at the tempo you set when it is stopped, and at the playing tempo when it plays.
Line-up buttons in the heads-up display are circles whenever they show only an icon.
Ripple and Drain no longer have the same icon: Ripple, which expands out, has its outer ring emphasized; Drain, which pulls in, keeps the inner ring emphasized.
The slider morph keeps its settings under its own name, so it no longer shares storage with the A | B habits animator.

Reverb tail no longer carries the slider morph. Changing the tail rebuilds the reverb, which waits for the slider to stop, so a swinging Tail did nothing you could hear and then rebuilt the reverb when it stopped. The other sliders keep the morph.

Tempo drift is now visible. It was working (it picks a new tempo at every pass of the lines, up to the percentage you set), but the tempo readout only ever showed the tempo you set. While the robot plays and the tempo drifts, the readout now shows the tempo that is actually playing, in the accent color. Stopped, or with drift at 0, it shows your set tempo. Note that drift only happens while the robot plays, and the tempo changes once per pass, so a slow tempo on a big grid drifts slowly.

The "clear the score" button (the slashed circle under the cube on the right rail) now shows only in edit mode, or while your finger plays the Field (where it clears field sounds). In normal play it is gone, so the "let go of all held notes" X can appear without pushing the rail down behind the tempo bar.
